title: Reverse Nodes In K Group
description: Given the head of a linked list, reverse the nodes of the list k at a time, and return the modified list. If the number of nodes is not a multiple of k then left-out nodes, in the end, should remain as they are.

steps.note: Starting `reverseKGroup` with head `[1,2,3,4,5]` and `k=2`. The list nodes are internally represented by their initial indices, with 0 being a dummy node.
Check for base cases: head (node 1) is not null and k (2) is not 1. Neither condition triggers a return.
Create a dummy node (index 0) to simplify list manipulations. Its `next` points to the original head (node 1).
`prevGroupEnd` (pointer `prev`) is initialized to the dummy node (index 0), which is the node before the first k-group.
Begin the `while(true)` loop to process k-groups.
`groupStart` (pointer `curr`) is set to `prevGroupEnd.next` (node 1).
`groupStart` (node 1) is not null. Proceed to find the k-th node.
`groupEnd` (pointer `j`) initially points to `groupStart` (node 1).
Start `for` loop to advance `groupEnd` by `k-1` steps. `i` starts at 1, loop for `i < k` (i.e., `i < 2`).
`groupEnd` (node 1) is not null. Continue.
Advance `groupEnd` to `groupEnd.next` (node 2).
Increment `i` to 2. The loop condition `i < k` (i.e., `2 < 2`) is now false. The `for` loop finishes. `groupEnd` is node 2.
`groupEnd` (node 2) is not null, indicating that a full k-group (nodes 1 and 2) exists.
`nextGroupStart` (node 3) stores the node immediately after the current k-group for later reconnection.
Cut the k-group from the rest of the list by setting `groupEnd.next` (node 2's next) to null. This isolates `(1->2)`.
Call `reverseList` helper function to reverse the current k-group, starting from `groupStart` (node 1). Pointers `prev`, `curr`, `j` reflect the main function's state.
Entering `reverseList` helper. The `head` for this helper is `groupStart` (node 1). Internal pointers for `reverseList` are initialized: `prev_rev` (null), `curr_rev` (node 1).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` (node 1) is not null.
`nextTemp` stores `curr_rev.next` (node 2) before `curr_rev.next` is modified.
`curr_rev.next` (node 1's next) is set to `prev_rev` (null).
`prev_rev` moves to `curr_rev` (node 1).
`curr_rev` moves to `nextTemp` (node 2).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` (node 2) is not null.
`nextTemp` stores `curr_rev.next` (null) before `curr_rev.next` is modified.
`curr_rev.next` (node 2's next) is set to `prev_rev` (node 1). List is now `2->1`.
`prev_rev` moves to `curr_rev` (node 2).
`curr_rev` moves to `nextTemp` (null).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` is null. Loop ends.
Returning `prev_rev` (node 2), which is the new head of the reversed sublist `(2->1)`.
Back in `reverseKGroup`. `prevGroupEnd.next` (dummy 0's next) is connected to `reversedHead` (node 2). The list segment is now `0->2->1`.
`groupStart` (node 1, now the tail of the reversed group) has its `next` connected to `nextGroupStart` (node 3). The list is `0->2->1->3->4->5`.
`prevGroupEnd` (pointer `prev`) is updated to `groupStart` (node 1) for the next iteration. This node will be the new tail of the previously reversed group.
Beginning next `while` loop iteration.
`groupStart` (pointer `curr`) is set to `prevGroupEnd.next` (node 3).
`groupStart` (node 3) is not null. Proceed.
`groupEnd` (pointer `j`) initially points to `groupStart` (node 3).
Start `for` loop to find the `k`-th node. `i` starts at 1.
`groupEnd` (node 3) is not null. Continue.
Advance `groupEnd` to `groupEnd.next` (node 4).
Increment `i` to 2. The loop condition `i < k` (i.e., `2 < 2`) is now false. The `for` loop finishes. `groupEnd` is node 4.
`groupEnd` (node 4) is not null, indicating a full k-group (nodes 3 and 4) exists.
`nextGroupStart` (node 5) stores the node immediately after the current k-group.
Cut the k-group from the rest of the list: `groupEnd.next` (node 4's next) is set to null. This isolates `(3->4)`.
Call `reverseList` to reverse the current k-group, starting from `groupStart` (node 3).
Entering `reverseList` helper. `head` for `reverseList` is node 3. Internal pointers: `prev_rev` (null), `curr_rev` (node 3).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` (node 3) is not null.
`nextTemp` stores `curr_rev.next` (node 4) before `curr_rev.next` is modified.
`curr_rev.next` (node 3's next) is set to `prev_rev` (null).
`prev_rev` moves to `curr_rev` (node 3).
`curr_rev` moves to `nextTemp` (node 4).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` (node 4) is not null.
`nextTemp` stores `curr_rev.next` (null) before `curr_rev.next` is modified.
`curr_rev.next` (node 4's next) is set to `prev_rev` (node 3). List is now `4->3`.
`prev_rev` moves to `curr_rev` (node 4).
`curr_rev` moves to `nextTemp` (null).
Inside `reverseList` loop: `curr_rev` is null. Loop ends.
Returning `prev_rev` (node 4), which is the new head of the reversed sublist `(4->3)`.
Back in `reverseKGroup`. `prevGroupEnd.next` (node 1's next) is connected to `reversedHead` (node 4). The list segment is now `1->4->3`.
`groupStart` (node 3, now the tail of the reversed group) has its `next` connected to `nextGroupStart` (node 5). The overall list is `0->2->1->4->3->5`.
`prevGroupEnd` (pointer `prev`) is updated to `groupStart` (node 3) for the next iteration.
Beginning next `while` loop iteration.
`groupStart` (pointer `curr`) is set to `prevGroupEnd.next` (node 5).
`groupStart` (node 5) is not null. Proceed.
`groupEnd` (pointer `j`) initially points to `groupStart` (node 5).
Start `for` loop to find the `k`-th node. `i` starts at 1.
`groupEnd` (node 5) is not null. Continue.
Advance `groupEnd` to `groupEnd.next` (null).

Increment `i` to 2. The loop condition `i < k` (i.e., `2 < 2`) is now false. The `for` loop finishes. `groupEnd` is null because node 5 is the last node, and there aren't enough nodes for a full k-group.
`groupEnd` is null. This means there are fewer than `k` nodes remaining (only node 5). According to the problem, these nodes should remain unreversed.
Break out of the main `while` loop.
Return `dummy.next` (node 2), which is the new head of the modified list. The final list is `2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5 -> null`.
